item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President immediately establishes executive-branch policy objectives for domestic medical supply chains, but neither changes legal rights nor mandates a specified later legal consequence.","evidence":"It is therefore the policy of the United States to"},{"segment_id":"2","code":2,"rationale":"Agencies must later conduct covered procurements using procedures that restrict competition to domestically produced products; the procurement consequence arises through agency implementation.","evidence":"using procedures to limit competition to only those Essential Medicines, Medical Countermeasures, and Critical Inputs that are produced in the United States"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must later develop and implement procurement strategies, but retain discretion over their contents and resulting contracts.","evidence":"develop and implement procurement strategies, including long-term contracts, consistent with law"},{"segment_id":"4","code":2,"rationale":"The Trade Representative must later modify federal procurement coverage to produce the specified exclusion for the listed products.","evidence":"modify United States Federal procurement product coverage under all relevant Free Trade Agreements and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement to exclude coverage"},{"segment_id":"5","code":2,"rationale":"The Trade Representative and Defense Secretary must later implement specified waiver modifications and procurement restrictions; the segment's exceptions delimit those mandated administrative outcomes.","evidence":"restrict the procurement of Essential Medicines, Medical Countermeasures, and Critical Inputs to domestic sources"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"An agency head who makes a covered determination must later provide an internal annual justification report to the President.","evidence":"shall submit an annual report to the President"},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"HHS and FDA must later review, consider, coordinate, recommend, and otherwise take appropriate action to identify and mitigate supply-chain vulnerabilities without a dictated legal outcome.","evidence":"shall take all necessary and appropriate action, consistent with law, to identify vulnerabilities"},{"segment_id":"8","code":2,"rationale":"HHS and FDA are directed to produce later legally consequential regulatory outcomes, including accelerated approvals or clearances and refusal of admission for qualifying imports.","evidence":"refuse admission, as appropriate, to imports of Essential Medicines, Medical Countermeasures, and Critical Inputs"},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"The Defense Secretary must prepare, transmit, and periodically update an interagency list, an internal planning and reporting function.","evidence":"shall provide to the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the FDA Commissioner, the Director of OMB, and the Director of the Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy a list"},{"segment_id":"10","code":1,"rationale":"EPA and HHS are directed to take appropriate action and exercise delegated prioritization and allocation authority as they deem necessary; the segment does not itself impose a consequence or dictate a particular later allocation.","evidence":"as the Secretary deems necessary or appropriate to promote the national defense"},{"segment_id":"11","code":1,"rationale":"Each agency head must periodically submit an internal report covering procurement history, expenditures, sources, and future planning.","evidence":"the head of each agency shall submit a report to the President"},{"segment_id":"12","code":1,"rationale":"The Commerce Secretary must later submit an internal status and recommendations report to specified executive officials.","evidence":"the Secretary of Commerce shall submit a report"}]}
